item.text: {"summary":"Publishable with one main weakness: the interval is mechanically coherent but rests on a very sparse, mismatched volatility sample rather than realized A-41 monthly or July-specific variation.","requiredFixes":[{"rubricItem":"interval","severity":"warning","summary":"The 80% interval half-width is derived from only two changes across sparse August 2023, August 2024, and June 2026 reference points, not realized month-to-month or July-relevant A-41 volatility.","actionRequested":"Either replace the volatility estimate with a small official A-41 monthly or same-month historical sample, or explicitly label the current sigma as a sparse proxy and justify why a 4.0 percentage-point 80% half-width is still appropriate."},{"rubricItem":"prior_update_interval","severity":"warning","summary":"The compact prior/update/interval step names the inputs and math, but the historical sample is too sparse to support the phrase 'larger shock than seen' with much force.","actionRequested":"Qualify the final sentence to say values outside the interval would exceed the limited fetched reference-class variation, or add a broader official-history sample."}],"optionalSuggestions":["Consider removing or downweighting the MarketWatch citation in favor of official archived BLS A-41 values if available.","The +0.1 point July/hybrid persistence adjustment is small enough to keep, but naming it as judgmental rather than model-estimated would improve clarity."]}
